method: git-tracked non-test source read from git archive at the recorded commits; one sample per rule (seed 20261101-<rule>, at most 15); one rater (the author) labelled every sampled hit explicitly. Informal: single rater, small samples. tp means a reviewer would agree the site could produce the rule's wrong behavior (torn record, duplicate effect after a reported failure, give-up on a transient failure) under a reachable condition.

status.two_write_append: cut: precision 0.50 (1 tp of 2 hits), below 0.7 (n=2; small sample, informal single rater)
status.failure_after_effect: cut: precision 0.00 (0 tp of 1 hit), below 0.7 (n=1; small sample, informal single rater)

status.timeout_terminal: cut: precision 0.00 (0 tp of 2 hits), below 0.7 (n=2; small sample, informal single rater). Measured after the quoted-key fix; both hits were a distinct non-timeout branch or a status the caller already treats as unknown

contamination: All four rules (three since cut) were designed after reading the hard-benchmark defects H01, H07 and H08 (evals/hard/private/oracles.json), so their recall on those cases is not evidence: two_write_append fires at H07 store.rs:1189 (window 1180-1191, agent-rally-point 25fc7e5); failure_after_effect fires at H08 lib.rs:1769 (window 1765-1780, babc9b0); sibling_retryable fires at H01 scan-lock.ts:458 (window 457-459, NavGator 3723d05); timeout_terminal (since cut) does not fire on H01 363-367 because that branch returns ok:false without a status or retryable field.

cut_rules_informal.two_write_append on Python file handles: not built: buffered text files usually flush a short record and its newline in one write
cut_rules_informal.sibling_retryable without a catch-all gu: any function mixing retryable true/false fired; 0/3 on NavGator scan-lock.ts after the fix (each false return was a distinct operational error)

sample.signal: record goes to a shared append file in more than one write call
sample.label: tp
sample.reason: writeln! on an unbuffered O_APPEND File writes the record and the newline separately; two watchers given the same --ack-file, or a reader tailing it, can see a torn or unterminated line

sample.signal: record goes to a shared append file in more than one write call
sample.label: fp
sample.reason: one-time migration runs under the room mutation lock, which every segment appender also takes, so no second writer can interleave

sample.reason: probe script aborts on an inbox contract violation; no caller retries the send, so a duplicate delivery cannot follow

sample.signal: timeout branch reports a terminal failure
sample.label: fp
sample.reason: the TimeoutExpired branch two lines up already returns state 'timeout'; this 'failed' belongs to the separate OSError branch (the command could not start), which is a real terminal launch failure

sample.signal: timeout branch reports a terminal failure
sample.label: fp
sample.reason: status 'error' is documented as 'harness failed (timeout, OSError)', distinct from 'contradicted'; the verdict never treats it as a failed claim, so the timeout stays an unknown outcome, not a terminal one
